subject: humanities
passage: Over the past two decades, English-language readers have encountered far more fiction translated from Korean than they once did. To some critics, this rise is simply one part of a broader boom in translated fiction of all kinds. Literary scholar Ines Halvorsen, who maintains a database of novels and story collections published in English translation, disagrees. The growth in Korean titles, she argues, has been so much faster than the growth of translated fiction as a whole that a general boom alone cannot account for it.

data.title: Fiction Titles Published in English Translation, Halvorsen Database

stem: Which choice most effectively uses data from the table to support Halvorsen's argument?

choices.A: In every year shown, titles translated from Korean made up a small fraction of all translated titles.
choices.B: The number of titles translated from Korean increased between each pair of years shown.
choices.C: From 2008 to 2023, translated fiction as a whole grew at a faster rate than fiction translated from Korean.
choices.D: From 2008 to 2023, Korean titles grew more than sevenfold, while all translated titles grew by about 15%.

explanation.why: Halvorsen's argument is a comparison of growth rates: Korean titles grew much faster than translated fiction overall. Support must therefore compare the growth of the two columns. Korean titles rose from 9 to 66, more than seven times as many, while all translated titles rose from 512 to 590, an increase of about 15%.
explanation.A: Incorrect. This is true, but the size of Korean fiction's share in any one year says nothing about how fast it grew compared with the whole.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is true, but it describes Korean titles alone; steady growth could still be part of a general boom if the total grew just as fast.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Korean titles grew more than sevenfold, while the total grew only about 15%, so this reverses the data.
explanation.D: Correct. It compares the growth of the two columns and shows Korean titles growing far faster than translated fiction as a whole.
